related_questions.question: Which at-home COVID test is most accurate?

text_blocks.snippet: While no at-home COVID test is 100% accurate, antigen tests are generally considered reliable when detecting positive cases, especially when symptoms are present. Positive results on antigen tests are highly accurate. However, they may be less sensitive than laboratory-based tests like PCR, particularly when viral load is low or during early infection.
Key points about at-home COVID tests:

list.title: Antigen tests:
list.snippet: These are rapid tests that detect specific proteins (antigens) from the virus. They are typically less sensitive than PCR tests but are convenient for at-home use and provide quick results.

list.title: PCR tests:
list.snippet: These are laboratory-based tests that detect the virus's genetic material. They are highly sensitive and accurate but require sending samples to a lab and take longer to produce results.

list.title: Sensitivity:
list.snippet: Antigen tests are less likely to detect the virus when viral load is low (e.g., early or late in infection, or in asymptomatic individuals).

list.title: Symptom presence:
list.snippet: At-home antigen tests are most effective when used by individuals with symptoms.

list.title: Accuracy of positive results:
list.snippet: Positive results from at-home antigen tests are generally reliable.

list.title: FDA-authorized tests:
list.snippet: The FDA has authorized several at-home OTC COVID-19 diagnostic tests, including tests by Maxim Biomedical, Mologic, Nano-Ditech, and Oceanit Foundry.
